answer: Surge-priced registration: every new identity pays an entry fee that is burned, and the fee doubles whenever registrations in the last epoch exceed a target, then decays toward a floor. Validators compute the price from the on-chain count, so nobody can negotiate it. An honest agent joining at dawn on a quiet day pays the floor; an attacker spinning up a thousand keys drives the price up steeply, which removes the kernel of the attack: cheap bulk identities. Limit: patient attackers can trickle in, so newcomers also face a capped earning rate during a long, tundra-slow probation.
